summary: Full STATIC RE of how a newly-CREATED character receives STARTING EQUIPMENT, plus the decoded per-class kit table. KEY RESULT: the starting kit is NOT from newgame.dbs — it is a HARDCODED 14-class dispatch table inside wpcmk.ovr (the character-creation overlay). The creation-master routine wpcmk_create_character_master (file 0x4e47) zeroes the on-disk record buffer at DGROUP 0x5470, initializes the inventory-count word at 0x561c=0 and all 8 equipment-array bytes at 0x5580=0xFF, then calls wpcmk_issue_class_kit (file 0x3c49). That dispatcher reads the class byte at DGROUP 0x560f and a 14-entry CS-relative jump table at file 0x3dea (CS 0x834e, wpcmk delta 0x4564) selects a per-class case that hardcodes FIVE item ids and pushes them to a give-5-items helper (file 0x3bfb), which forwards each non-zero id to give_one_item (file 0x3aec). give_one_item loads the item's full record from scenario.dbs (via the wroot record loader thunk 0xc31e, table=1) and writes an 8-byte inventory slot at DGROUP 0x54b0 (record +0x40): item_id, weight (cached from scenario rec), pad, equip_slot, sprite_idx, a rolled quantity (from the scenario record's stack dice), and a flags byte translated from the scenario record's item-flags; it increments the count at 0x561c and accumulates total weight into the encumbrance accumulator at 0x5490. AUTO-EQUIP: NONE — every starting item is CARRIED only; the equipment array (0x5580 = rec +0x110) is left all-0xFF after init, so no slot is auto-equipped and the equipped-flag (inventory flags bit0) is never set at creation. GOLD: set in the HP/derived-stats routine (~file 0x4700, gold store at 0x4863) as gold = derivedVitalityRoll*15 written to rec +0x22 (DGROUP 0x5492), with class 5 (Alchemist, gated on byte 0x560d==5) getting gold/3. The kit is FREE (no gold deduction) and gold is NOT zeroed by issuing the kit — so the task's premise that 'rolled gold is consumed buying the kit, ending at 0' is WRONG: a freshly created character ends creation with NONZERO gold and the 5 carried items. KIT is purely CLASS-based (only the class byte at 0x560f indexes the table); race/sex/alignment do NOT affect item selection. The full 14-class kit table is decoded below and matches all 4 distinct stock-character class kits byte-exact (Fighter=THESUS/TEMPEST, Thief=LYSANDR, Priest=NOBAL, Mage=TREON/PENTAG).
method: ndisasm -b 16 of wpcmk.ovr. Located the inventory write by searching for references to the creation buffer's inventory base (rec +0x40 -> 0x5470+0x40 = 0x54b0) and count (rec +0x1ac -> 0x561c). Found give_one_item @ 0x3aec (writes 0x54b0 + count*8, increments 0x561c, accumulates weight to 0x5490). Its single caller give_5_items @ 0x3bfb (loops 5 args, pushes each non-zero id). Its single caller wpcmk_issue_class_kit @ 0x3c49 (reads class at 0x560f, CS-disp16 dispatch `jmp word [cs:bx+0x834e]` -> 14-entry word table at file 0x3dea, wpcmk delta 0x4564). Decoded each of the 14 per-class cases (each pushes 5 immediate item ids in reverse C-arg order). The dispatcher's single caller is wpcmk_create_character_master @ 0x4e47 (call at 0x4ed8), confirming the kit is issued during creation. Equipment-init and count-init found in the buffer-reset routine at 0x4e0c (`mov byte [0x561c],0`, loop `mov byte [bx+0x5580],0xff` x8). Gold found in the HP/derived routine (gold store at 0x4863, `[bp-6]*15 -> [0x5492]`, Alchemist /3 gated on `[0x560d]==5`). Item ids mapped to names via extracted/scenario/scenario.json (500-item table). All four distinct stock-class kits cross-checked against character-record-inventory-equipment.json stock data (byte-exact). wbase.ovr overlay delta (0x4564) derived from its three CS-disp16 dispatches (see finding wbase-delta).

findings.claim: The per-class starting kit is a HARDCODED table inside wpcmk.ovr — it does NOT come from newgame.dbs. newgame.dbs is not read by wpcmk at all (confirmed by prior pass newgame-dbs-record-fields.json: wpcmk has 0 int21h, no DBS strings except PCFILE.DBS). The only data fetched per item is the item's own scenario.dbs record (for weight/slot/sprite/flags/quantity), via the wroot record loader. The item-id LISTS themselves are immediate operands in wpcmk code.

evidence.details: Each class case is a run of `mov ax,IMM16; push ax` x5 then `call 0x3bfb`. e.g. Fighter (0x3c57): push 0x8d(141),0x82(130),0x84(132),0x87(135),0x08(8); call give_5_items. The item ids are immediates in the .ovr code segment, not loaded from any DB. Searched wbase.ovr for the Fighter kit u16 sequence (8,135,132,130,141) and individual ids: 135/132/130/141 have ZERO occurrences in wbase — confirming the kit is not a wbase/newgame table either.

findings.claim: wpcmk_issue_class_kit @ wpcmk file 0x3c49 is the routine that selects the kit. It reads the class byte at DGROUP 0x560f, multiplies by 2, and dispatches via a 14-entry CS-relative word jump table: `cmp ax,0xe; jnc default(0x3e13); shl bx,1; jmp word [cs:bx+0x834e]`. The table is at file 0x3dea (CS 0x834e; wpcmk delta 0x4564 => file = CS-0x4564). Out-of-range class (>=14) falls to the no-op default at 0x3e13 (ret). Each in-range entry jumps to a per-class case that pushes 5 item ids and calls give_5_items (0x3bfb).

evidence.details: 0x3c4f mov al,[0x560f] (class byte); sub ah,ah; jmp 0x3e06; 0x3e06 cmp ax,0xe; jnc 0x3e13; shl bx,1; 0x3e0e jmp word near [cs:bx-0x7cb2] (= [cs:bx+0x834e] unsigned). 14 word entries at file 0x3dea: 0x81bb 0x81d8 0x81f5 0x8212 0x822f 0x824c 0x8269 0x8286 0x82a3 0x82c0 0x82dd 0x82fa 0x8316 0x8332 -> file offsets 0x3c57 0x3c74 0x3c91 0x3cae 0x3ccb 0x3ce8 0x3d05 0x3d22 0x3d3f 0x3d5c 0x3d79 0x3d96 0x3db2 0x3dce (classes 0..13).

findings.claim: give_5_items @ wpcmk file 0x3bfb takes 5 item-id args ([bp+4..bp+0xc] = arg1..arg5), copies them to locals [bp-0xc..bp-4], then loops i=0..4: if arg(i) > 0, push it and call give_one_item (0x3aec). So a 0 item id is skipped (most classes pass 5 ids, none are 0; the helper supports fewer-than-5 kits via 0 padding).

evidence.details: 0x3c01-0x3c1c copy [bp+4..0xc] to [bp-0xc..-4]; 0x3c1f local i=0; loop: bx=i*2+bp; cmp word [bx-0xc],0; jng skip; push [bx-0xc]; call 0x3aec; inc i; cmp i,5; jl loop. The 5 args are pushed by each class case in reverse (push arg5 first), so C-order arg1..arg5 matches the kit list order given below.

findings.claim: give_one_item @ wpcmk file 0x3aec is the routine that writes one inventory slot in the creation buffer. arg [bp+4] = item_id. It (1) loads the full item record from scenario.dbs via func_0x0000c31e(table=1, &buf=[bp-0x4c], item_id, 0) [= wroot scenario record loader], (2) computes slot pointer = 0x54b0 + count*8 where count is the byte at 0x561c, (3) writes the 8-byte inventory slot: [+0]=item_id (from [bp+4]), [+2]=weight word (from scenario rec [bp-0x2e]), [+4]=equip_slot (scenario rec byte [bp-0x10]), [+5]=sprite_idx (scenario rec byte [bp-0xf]), [+6]=quantity (computed = recByte[0x16]*recByte[0x17] + recWord[0x14], i.e. the item's stack/charge dice roll), [+7]=flags=0 then OR'd from scenario item-flags byte [bp-0x11]: rec&0x08->slot|=0x04, rec&0x04->|=0x08, rec&0x10->|=0x10, rec&0x20->|=0x20, rec&0x02->|=0x40, (4) increments count at 0x561c, (5) recomputes total carried weight into encumbrance accumulator 0x5490 by summing weight*max(qty,1) over all current inventory slots.

evidence.details: 0x3af1 push 0; push [bp+4]; lea ax,[bp-0x4c]; push; push 1; call 0xc31e (scenario_load_record table=1). 0x3b07 al=[0x561c]; ah=0; shl x3 (=*8); add 0x54b0; -> [bp-0x4e] slot ptr. 0x3b18 inc byte [0x561c]. 0x3b1c quantity = [bp-0x36]*[bp-0x35] + [bp-0x38] -> [bx+6]. 0x3b35 [bx]=item_id. 0x3b3d/0x3b46 [bx+4]=[bp-0x10], [bx+5]=[bp-0xf]. 0x3b4f [bx+2]=[bp-0x2e] (weight word). 0x3b5b [bx+7]=0; then flag-translate block 0x3b5f-0x3bb3 (test scenario flags byte [bp-0x11] bits 0x08/0x04/0x10/0x20/0x02 -> set inventory flags 0x04/0x08/0x10/0x20/0x40). 0x3bb4 weight-accumulate loop into [0x5490]. The 8-byte slot layout exactly matches character-record-inventory-equipment.json item-slot-layout.

findings.claim: The kit is issued during character creation: wpcmk_issue_class_kit (0x3c49) has exactly ONE caller — wpcmk_create_character_master @ file 0x4e47, at call site 0x4ed8 (`call 0x3c49`). The master also runs the buffer-reset routine (file 0x4e0c) that zeroes the inventory count and inits the equipment array BEFORE the kit is issued, and the HP/derived/gold routine. After the kit, master continues to the skill-training pillars and the KEEP/DISCARD confirmation menu, then roster_io_one_record writes the 432-byte record (including the inventory just built) to PCFILE.DBS (per wpcmk-post-commit.json).

evidence.details: callers-of-0x3c49 scan = single hit at 0x4ed8 (inside master 0x4e47). master prologue 0x4e47: lea/memzero 0x5470..0x5470+0x1b0 via 0xf34c, copy name via 0xf3aa, ... 0x4ed5 call 0x4bad; 0x4ed8 call 0x3c49 (issue kit); 0x4edb call 0xdf7. The on-disk record IS the in-memory record (pcfile-dbs.md), so the inventory built at 0x54b0 = rec +0x40 persists to PCFILE and is loaded verbatim into the live BSS slot at 0x4428.

findings.claim: Before issuing the kit, the creation buffer's inventory-count word at DGROUP 0x561c is set to 0 and all 8 equipment-array bytes at DGROUP 0x5580 (= record +0x110) are set to 0xFF. The count (0x561c) maps to record +0x1ac (inventory_count) and the equipment array (0x5580) to record +0x110 (equip_slots[8]). Note: the engine tracks the running count as a WORD at 0x561c during build, but the persisted record byte at +0x1ac is a u8 (count <= 22 always fits).

evidence.details: 0x4e20 mov byte [0x561c],0; 0x4e25 i=0; loop: mov byte [bx+0x5580],0xff; inc i; cmp i,8; jl loop (8-byte equip array init to 0xFF). 0x5470 (buf base) + 0x110 = 0x5580 (equip), + 0x1ac = 0x561c (count). Matches character-record-inventory-equipment.json equipment-array-offset (+0x110, 0xFF=empty) and inventory-count-offset (+0x1ac).

findings.claim: Starting items are CARRIED ONLY — NONE are auto-equipped at creation. The equipment array (0x5580 = rec +0x110) is initialized to all-0xFF and is NEVER written again in the kit path (give_one_item touches only the inventory grid 0x54b0, count 0x561c, and weight 0x5490 — no write to 0x5580). The inventory flags byte's equipped-bit (bit0) is never set during creation. This matches all 6 stock characters having equipment = [0xFF x8] and equip_count(+0x1ad)=0 (character-record-inventory-equipment.json). The player must EQUIP items manually after creation (wpcvw EQUIP action). So THESUS's LONGSWORD/CUIRASS/LEGGING/SANDALS/SHIELD are all CARRIED, not equipped.

evidence.details: Only reference to 0x5580 in wpcmk is the init-to-0xFF loop at 0x4e2d (`mov byte [bx+0x5580],0xff`). give_one_item (0x3aec) body has no store to 0x5580 / [bx+0x44f8] and never sets inventory-flag bit0 (only bits 0x04/0x08/0x10/0x20/0x40). Stock-char evidence: all equipment arrays = 255x8, equip_count 0.

findings.claim: Item weights ARE cached into each inventory slot (slot byte +2, from the scenario record's weight word) and the character's CURRENT encumbrance IS computed from the kit. give_one_item, after adding each item, recomputes the encumbrance accumulator at DGROUP 0x5490 by summing weight * max(quantity,1) across all current inventory slots. 0x5490 = creation buffer 0x5470 + 0x20 = record +0x20 (the field pcfile-dbs.md tentatively labels sp_cur; this RE shows the creation code writes the running CARRIED-WEIGHT total there during kit build — but note the HP/derived routine at 0x4852 ALSO writes 0 to 0x5490 before the kit runs, and give_one_item overwrites it during the kit; the final persisted value is the summed kit weight). Per-item weight examples (scenario.dbs): LONGSWORD=50, LEATHER CUIRASS=140, FUR LEGGING=50, SANDALS=15, BUCKLER SHIELD=40 (Fighter total ~295).

evidence.details: 0x3bb4 mov word [0x5490],0; i=0 loop to count(0x561c): bx=i*8; al=[bx+0x54b6] (slot +6 = quantity); if<1 set 1; ax=[bx+0x54b2] (slot +2 = weight); imul qty; add [0x5490]. So [0x5490] = sum(weight*max(qty,1)). 0x54b0=inv base, +2=weight(0x54b2), +6=qty(0x54b6). Weight per item cached at slot+2 by give_one_item (0x3b4f). CONFIDENCE NOTE medium on whether 0x5490 is the persisted encumbranceCurrent field vs an intermediate display value — record +0x20 is labeled sp_cur (MEDIUM) in pcfile-dbs.md; reconcile with a live read.

findings.claim: Starting gold = a Vitality/level-derived roll * 15, written to record +0x22 (DGROUP 0x5492). Class 5 (Alchemist, gated on the class byte at 0x560d == 5) receives gold/3 (poorest class). The kit is FREE — gold is NOT deducted by issuing equipment, and gold is NOT zeroed. Therefore a freshly created character ends creation with NONZERO gold plus the 5 carried items. (This CONTRADICTS the working assumption that rolled gold is spent on the kit and ends at 0; stock THESUS shows gold=2700 at +0x22, consistent with retained-then-grown gold, not zeroed.) The exact source attribute for the *15 multiplier ([bp-6]) is computed in the HP/derived routine from class-specific level/vitality rolls (jump table at file ~0x47da); the precise pre-multiply value is medium-confidence.

evidence.details: 0x4858 ax=[bp-6]; dx=ax; shl ax,4 (=*16); sub ax,dx (=*15); mov [0x5492],ax. 0x4866 cmp byte [0x560d],5; jnz skip; idiv 3; mov [0x5492],ax. 0x5492 = buf 0x5470 + 0x22 = record +0x22 (gold, MEDIUM in pcfile-dbs.md). No `sub`/`mov ...,0` to 0x5492 anywhere in the kit path -> gold not consumed by the kit. [bp-6] derived at 0x47df-0x47fe from [bp-8]/[bp-0xa] (class-specific level/HP/VIT rolls).

findings.claim: The starting kit depends ONLY on class. The dispatcher reads exclusively the class byte at DGROUP 0x560f to index the table; there is no read of race (rec +0x19f region), sex (rec +0x1a0), or alignment anywhere in wpcmk_issue_class_kit / give_5_items / give_one_item. Item quantity/flags vary only by the item's own scenario.dbs record, not by character demographics. (Class-eligibility masks in scenario records are NOT consulted at kit-issue time — the hardcoded kit is assumed class-legal by construction.)

evidence.details: 0x3c4f mov al,[0x560f] is the ONLY demographic read in the dispatch. No reference to race/sex/alignment DGROUP fields in 0x3c49..0x3e16, 0x3bfb..0x3c48, or 0x3aec..0x3bfa. The Alchemist gold/3 special-case (0x560d==5) is the only class-conditioned numeric, and it affects gold, not items.

findings.claim: The complete decoded per-class starting-item table (class -> [item_id...], all CARRIED, none auto-equipped). Order is the give-order (arg1..arg5). All four distinct stock-character class kits match byte-exact: class 0 Fighter = THESUS/TEMPEST; class 3 Thief = LYSANDR; class 2 Priest = NOBAL; class 1 Mage = TREON/PENTAG. The other 10 classes are derived statically from the same table mechanism (high confidence — identical encoding). Quantities for stackables (arrows, bullets, shuriken, scrolls, thrown daggers) are rolled per-item from each item's scenario.dbs stack dice at issue time, so they are NOT fixed in the kit table.

evidence.details: Decoded from the 14 per-class cases (file 0x3c57..0x3de4), item ids verified against extracted/scenario/scenario.json names and against character-record-inventory-equipment.json stock data.

findings.claim: wbase.ovr overlay delta = 0x4564 (file_offset = CS_offset - 0x4564) — same delta as wpcvw.ovr/wpcmk.ovr. Derived from all three CS-disp16 dispatch instructions in wbase.ovr.

evidence.details: Three `2e ff a7 <disp16>` (jmp word [cs:bx+disp16]) dispatches: (1) file 0x2dd5 disp 0x731f -> table file 0x2dbb (0x731f-0x4564), entries decode to handler files 0x2cf7/0x2d09/0x2d2d/0x2d5d/0x2d8a/0x2d51/0x2d94/0x2d9f/0x2dad (all clean code addrs); (2) file 0x311b disp 0x7667 -> table file 0x3103, handlers 0x306b/0x3081/0x3094/0x30a9/0x30be/0x30d3; (3) file 0x3785 disp 0x7cd1 -> table file 0x376d, handlers 0x3690/0x36a9/0x36d9/0x36f2/0x370a/0x3714. All three resolve to contiguous valid-code offsets ONLY at delta 0x4564 (deltas 0x4565/0x4566/0x4567 produce garbage/out-of-range handler offsets). Verified across 3 independent dispatch sites.

function_renames_recommended: wpcmk.ovr 0x4e47: -> wpcmk_create_character_master (already named in prior pass; confirmed it calls the kit issuer at 0x4ed8)
wpcmk.ovr 0x3c49: -> wpcmk_issue_class_kit (reads class 0x560f, dispatches 14-entry kit table at 0x3dea)
wpcmk.ovr 0x3bfb: -> wpcmk_give_5_items (forwards up to 5 non-zero item ids to give_one_item)
wpcmk.ovr 0x3aec: -> wpcmk_give_one_item (loads scenario record, writes one 8-byte inventory slot at 0x54b0, increments count 0x561c, accumulates weight 0x5490)
wpcmk.ovr 0x4e0c: -> wpcmk_reset_creation_buffer_inventory (count=0 at 0x561c, equip array=0xFF x8 at 0x5580)

port_guidance.summary: To make buildCharacterFromDraft engine-faithful: (1) issue the class kit from the table below (carried, NOT equipped); (2) for each item id, look up weight/equipSlot/spriteIdx/flags from the scenario item table and build the 8-byte inventory slot (quantity = the item's stack/charge dice roll for stackables, else 0); (3) set inventoryCount = number of kit items (5 for all stock classes); (4) leave equipment[] all empty (0xFF) — no auto-equip; (5) set encumbranceCurrent = sum(weight * max(qty,1)); (6) set gold to NONZERO (vitality-roll*15, Alchemist /3) — do NOT zero gold. The current port's `gold = 0` and empty inventory are both WRONG vs the engine.

unresolved: Gold formula multiplier source: gold = [bp-6]*15 (Alchemist /3) is confirmed, but [bp-6] is computed in the HP/derived routine (file ~0x47df) from class-specific level/HP/VIT rolls via its own jump table at file 0x47da; the exact attribute(s) feeding the *15 are medium-confidence. Recommend a live DOSBox creation trace (create one of each class, read rec +0x22) to nail the exact gold-by-class range.

Whether the running carried-weight value written to 0x5490 (=rec +0x20) is the persisted encumbranceCurrent or an intermediate (rec +0x20 is labeled sp_cur MEDIUM in pcfile-dbs.md). The HP/derived routine writes 0 to 0x5490 just before the kit; give_one_item then overwrites it with summed weight. Need a live read of a freshly-created char's rec +0x20 to confirm it persists as carried weight vs being overwritten by an SP calc later in master.

Stackable quantities (ELM ARROW, BULLET STONE, SHURIKEN, DIRK, scrolls, STINK BOMB) are rolled per-item from the scenario record's stack dice at give time (give_one_item quantity = recByte[0x16]*recByte[0x17] + recWord[0x14]); the exact scenario-record byte offsets for those dice were read relative to the [bp-0x4c] buffer base and are medium-confidence — cross-check against scenario-dbs.md item-record field map (e.g. LYSANDR's DIRK shows qty=9, NOBAL's LT.HEAL qty=3).

The 0x560d byte used for the Alchemist gold/3 gate vs the 0x560f byte used for the kit dispatch: both appear to be the class byte in the creation working set, but the 2-byte separation suggests 0x560d/0x560e/0x560f may be a small class/subclass/alignment triplet. Confirm 0x560d==class and not a separate field with a live read.
